newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: YTL Power seeks to list China, Africa units.
newsitem.headline: YTL Power seeks to list China, Africa units.

text.p: YTL Power International Bhd said on Monday it is seeking to list the subsidiaries of its Chinese and African subsidiaries.
"We want to list the subsidiaries of YTL Power depending on market condition," YTL Power managing director Francis Yeoh Sock Ping told a news briefing.
"There is agreement with our partners to do that. We want to list the pan China company (YTL CPI)," he said, adding, "We could do a simultaneous listing in Harare (of Africa Power Ltd)."
"The strategy is to list YTL CPI on the market subject to (market) conditions," Yeoh said. "The listings are one of our options for financing (power projects)," he added.

YTL Power has a 51 percent stake in YTL-CPI, the joint venture company with China Power Investment Holding Co Ltd. YTL Power and CPI have signed a joint venture pact to develop and own power generation facilities in Nanchang, Jiangxi province.

"The Nanchang power project...has secured the formal approval of the State Economic and Trade Commission (known as the Lixiang) after consultation with the State Planning Commission and the Ministry of Electric Power of the PRC," YTL Power said in a statement.
The project comprises the acquisition of two 125 MW existing coal-fired generating units and the construction of a new 300 MW coal-fired plant, the statement said.
Yeoh said that the acquisition of the two plants would immediately add to YTL Power's turnover, but did not say by how much. In calendar 1996, YTL Power reported sales of 1.15 billion ringgit.
YTL Power's subsidiary YTL CPI Power Ltd holds a 60 pct stake in the project. The balance of 40 percent is held by the Jiangxi provincial government.
YTL Power said the state's approval would result in the allocation of 480 million renminbi to fund the new 300 MW unit and to upgrade the current transmission facilities.

The African project involves a letter of intent between YTL Power and the government of Zimbabwe to privatise the 920 MW Hwange Power Station through joint venture company Africa Power Ltd, which is 51 percent owned by YTL Power.
The balance is owned by Zimbabwe Electricity Supply Authority (ZESA), Zimbabwe's utility board.
Yeoh said the approval of the Zimbabwe Hwange acquisition was "at a very advanced stage", but declined to give details.
